channel.title: How to verify running Kicksecure version?
channel.description:
Hi Guys, relatively new to this . .
I did an inplace upgrade from 18.2.1.9 to 18.2.4.2.
Would like to verify 18.2.4.2 is the actual running version. Failed to find a way.
Any help would be greatly appriciated.
Cheers,

item.title: How to verify running Kicksecure version?
item.dc:creator: arraybolt3
item.description:
I’m not sure how this could be done in a way that is particularly valuable. Knowing the build version you are effectively running might be useful to ensure you aren’t missing updates, but embedding the latest point release version into a package won’t do that, all it will do is tell you that you have a new enough version of that specific package installed. The best way to tell if you have all updates installed is to run systemcheck, which will tell you if you have Kicksecure repos enabled and if there are any updates available. If you have Kicksecure repos enabled and there are no updates available, then you have everything installed and don’t need to worry (unless of course you’re running an EOL major version of Kicksecure). I’m not sure what other use an updating build version number would have.

Right now if you search for Kicksecure in the start menu the setup wizard distribution shows up which is okay but in addition it should also shows a result called Kicksecure or Whonix which shows the installed version depending on the OS it is running.

This page may be helpful:

Kicksecure – 13 May 26

Point Release

What is a Point Release?

Installing any version of Kicksecure 18 and fully updating it leads to a system which is (mostly) identical to installing a Kicksecure point release.

If the Kicksecure installation is updated, no further action is required.
